headline: EU Regulatory Briefing: Green Claims Withdrawal, Right to Repair, CSRD Preparation
summary: Reports indicate the European Commission plans to scrap the proposed Green Claims Directive. Meanwhile, the EU Right to Repair law has taken effect alongside new consultations on repairability rules. With revised ESRS standards entering into force on 10 November, preparation for CSRD reporting starting in financial year 2027 remains essential.

items.title: Commission Reportedly Scraps Proposed Green Claims Directive
items.what: Reports state the European Commission intends to withdraw the proposed Green Claims Directive and its independent verification requirement.
items.meaning: Your consumer marketing for power tools will not face ex-ante verification under this directive, though general greenwashing prohibitions still apply.
items.action: Review environmental marketing strategies against existing EU unfair commercial practice rules.

items.title: Right to Repair Law Takes Effect Alongside New Consultation
items.what: The Right to Repair law took effect on 1 November, while the Commission launched a public consultation on stronger repairability rules.
items.meaning: As a brand manufacturer of consumer equipment, spare part accessibility and repairability standards directly impact product design and post-sale service.
items.action: Assess spare parts availability and evaluate participation in the public consultation.

items.title: Revised ESRS Standard Set to Enter into Force
items.what: The revised ESRS standards enter into force on 10 November 2026 following Omnibus reform updates to ESG disclosure obligations.
items.meaning: Meeting the employee and turnover thresholds places your business inside CSRD scope starting in financial year 2027.
items.action: Align Chinese supplier sustainability data collection with the finalized ESRS disclosure framework.

items.title: Rules Detailed for Crediting Third-Country Carbon Prices Under CBAM
items.what: New details outline rules for crediting carbon prices paid in third countries under CBAM, alongside reported discussions on UK exemptions.
items.meaning: While finished tools fall outside direct CBAM import filings, Chinese supplier carbon pricing crediting may influence upstream component costs.
items.action: Monitor supplier energy cost shifts and potential future expansions of CBAM product scope.
